comment: Request/response leads (0.57.0): CSRF candidates, upload and auth-flow endpoints, mass assignment and sensitive response fields, JWT claims. Every *Names/*Fields/*Headers regex is matched against a WHOLE name, case-insensitive. authFlows are found (not matched) in the request path, case-insensitive; 'note' becomes the finding's Try hint. Keep every span bounded (ReDoS).

authFlows.name: login
authFlows.note: compare responses for a valid vs an invalid username (account enumeration), send the same request 20-30 times to see whether a lockout / rate limit / CAPTCHA kicks in, and try SQLi/NoSQLi in the credentials

authFlows.name: OTP / MFA
authFlows.note: check whether the code can be brute-forced (no attempt limit), reused, or skipped by calling the next step directly; flip a success flag in the response (false -> true) and see whether the client proceeds

authFlows.name: password reset
authFlows.note: change the target account (id/email) between steps, inject a Host / X-Forwarded-Host header to poison the reset link, and check whether reset tokens are predictable, reusable or leaked in the response

authFlows.name: signup
authFlows.note: re-register an existing id/email with different case or trailing spaces, add role/isAdmin/grade fields to the body (mass assignment), and check whether verification steps can be skipped

authFlows.name: token refresh
authFlows.note: replay an old / already-used refresh token, swap in another user's token, and check whether logging out actually invalidates it
